chapters.title: Chapter 4: The Cost of Getting It Wrong

lessons.title: Interest for Not Paying or Underpaying Advance Tax

body.text: If, by 31 March, you have paid less than 90% of the tax you owe after TDS, the law charges interest of 1% for every month, or part of a month, from 1 April until you pay the balance. The meter starts on 1 April and stops only when you pay, which is why a few weeks of delay in filing can cost real money.

children.text: Chapter 3 was about paying on time. This chapter is about what it costs when you do not. There are two separate interest charges for advance tax, and they are often confused. This lesson covers the first: interest for not paying advance tax, or paying too little of it by the end of the year. The next lesson covers interest for missing or short-paying individual instalments.

markDefs.definition: Tax on the total income finally determined, when your return is processed or assessed, reduced by TDS, TCS and any relief or tax credits. It is not your estimate, and it is not tax before TDS.

children.text: Section 424 of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (old section 234B) applies to anyone liable to pay advance tax who either paid none, or paid less than 90% of their

. Interest is simple interest at 1% a month on the shortfall, from 1 April following the tax year until the date your total income is determined, but for any amount you pay as self-assessment tax, it stops on the date of that payment.

body.title: Quick Check: The 90% Trap
body.question: Rajan's assessed tax for tax year 2026-27 is ₹3,00,000. By 31 March 2027 he paid ₹2,65,000 of advance tax, and he pays the balance as self-assessment tax on 20 July 2027. How much interest under section 424 does he owe?
options: Nil, because he paid most of his tax
₹1,400, on the full ₹35,000 shortfall for 4 months
body.explanation: ₹2,65,000 is about 88.3% of ₹3,00,000, below the 90% line, so interest applies on the whole shortfall of ₹35,000, not just the part below 90%. From 1 April to 20 July is 4 months, counting July as a full month. ₹35,000 × 1% × 4 = ₹1,400. Had he paid ₹2,75,000, about 91.7%, no section 424 interest would apply at all.

children.text: What It Costs to Pay Nothing

Nisha is a freelance brand strategist in Indore who keeps regular books. Her tax for tax year 2026-27, after the little TDS a few corporate clients deducted, is ₹2,00,000. She pays no advance tax at all, then pays the full ₹2,00,000 as self-assessment tax on 25 July 2027 just before filing.

children.text: This is only the first of her two interest charges. Because she also missed all four instalments, interest for deferment under section 425 applies on top. The next lesson works that out for her.

body.label: Nisha's interest for not paying advance tax
body.context: 4% of her tax, for paying in July rather than by March. It is not deductible, and it rises by ₹2,000 for every extra month she waits.

body.title: Section 424 interest on a ₹2,00,000 shortfall, by month of payment after the tax year

children.text: The chart makes the trade-off plain. Every month of delay adds the same amount, so there is no reason to hold back a known balance. If you know in April that you underpaid, pay the self-assessment tax in April, not when you get round to filing in July.

body.title: Try It: A Short Payment Settled in August
body.prompt: Varun, a Jaipur-based physiotherapist who keeps regular books, has assessed tax of ₹1,20,000 for tax year 2026-27. He paid ₹1,00,000 of advance tax by 15 March 2027 and pays the balance on 5 August 2027. How much interest under section 424 does he owe? Answer in rupees.
body.explanation: 90% of ₹1,20,000 is ₹1,08,000, and he paid only ₹1,00,000, so section 424 applies. The shortfall is ₹20,000. From 1 April to 5 August is 5 months (April to August, with August counted in full). ₹20,000 × 1% × 5 = ₹1,000. Paying ₹8,000 more by 15 March would have avoided this interest entirely.

body.title: Fill in the Blank: The Threshold
body.textWithBlank: Interest under section 424 applies if the advance tax you paid is less than ___% of your assessed tax.
body.explanation: The line is 90% of assessed tax, meaning tax on your finally determined income less TDS, TCS and relief. Below it, interest runs on the whole shortfall. As an example of the rounding rule, a shortfall of ₹1,52,380 paid in June is taken as ₹1,52,300, giving interest of ₹4,569 for 3 months.

children.text: Section 424 and Section 425 Are Separate Charges

body.title: Two interest charges, two different questions

columns.label: Section 424 (old 234B)
points: Question: did you pay at least 90% of your tax by 31 March?
Runs from 1 April until you pay the balance or income is determined
Can run for many months if you delay

columns.label: Section 425 (old 234C)
points: Question: did you pay enough by each of the four due dates?
Measured against tax due on returned income
Fixed at 3 months per instalment shortfall, and 1 month for March

children.text: A taxpayer can owe both, either, or neither. Paying 100% on 15 March avoids section 424 completely but may still leave section 425 interest for the earlier dates. Paying every instalment on time but grossly underestimating income can do the reverse.

body.text: Filing late adds a third charge. If you file after the due date with tax still unpaid, section 423 (old 234A) charges 1% a month on the unpaid tax from the due date. And none of these interest amounts can be claimed as a deduction against income. When you owe self-assessment tax, the cheapest date to pay it is the earliest one.

body.title: Scenario: Mahesh Misses His FD Interest
body.scenario: Mahesh runs a textile trading business in Surat and keeps regular books. He paid ₹2,40,000 of advance tax for tax year 2026-27, based on business profit alone. In June 2027, while preparing his return, his accountant finds ₹1.3 lakh of FD interest in AIS that nobody had included. His assessed tax after TDS turns out to be ₹2,80,000.
body.prompt: Does section 424 interest apply? How much does it cost if he pays the balance in July 2027, and how much if he waits and files a belated return in December 2027?
body.modelAnswer: Yes. 90% of ₹2,80,000 is ₹2,52,000, and he paid only ₹2,40,000, about 85.7%. That puts him ₹12,000 below the line, so interest applies on the full shortfall of ₹40,000. If he pays the balance as self-assessment tax in July 2027, that is 4 months from 1 April: ₹40,000 × 1% × 4 = ₹1,600. If he delays to December 2027, it is 9 months: ₹3,600, plus interest for late filing under section 423 on the unpaid tax from the due date, plus a late filing fee. There may also be interest under section 425 for his instalments. The practical answer is to pay the ₹40,000 the day the error is found, file on time, and add a line to next year's estimation worksheet for FD interest from AIS.

body.title: Three Habits That Prevent Default Interest
steps: In the first week of March, do a full estimate including every AIS entry, not just your main income
Make sure advance tax paid by 15 March, or at the latest 31 March, is at least 90% of the tax you expect to owe after TDS, and aim for 100%
In early April, compare AIS and your final figures; if there is a shortfall, pay self-assessment tax immediately rather than at filing time

body.label: Section 424: Interest for Defaults in Payment of Advance Tax
body.description: Text and explanation of section 424 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, which replaces section 234B of the 1961 Act.

cards.definition: Interest at 1% a month when advance tax paid is less than 90% of assessed tax, from 1 April until the balance is paid or income is determined.
Tax on finally determined income, less TDS, TCS, relief and tax credits.
If advance tax paid is 90% or more of assessed tax, section 424 interest does not apply at all.
Below 90%, interest runs on the entire gap between assessed tax and advance tax paid.
The shortfall is rounded down to the nearest ₹100, and part of a month counts as a full month.
Separate interest for filing the return late with tax unpaid.

points: Section 424 charges 1% a month when advance tax paid by 31 March is less than 90% of assessed tax
Once below 90%, interest runs on the entire shortfall, not just the part below 90%
Interest starts on 1 April and, for amounts paid as self-assessment tax, stops on the date of payment; part of a month counts as a full month
Every month of delay adds the same amount, so pay any known balance as early as possible
Section 424 is separate from section 425 interest on instalments and section 423 interest for late filing; you can owe all three
Interest on tax is never deductible, so avoiding it is a pure saving

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and does not constitute tax, legal or investment advice. Section references are to the Income-tax Act, 2025, with the corresponding Income-tax Act, 1961 section in brackets. Examples are simplified, assume a single self-assessment payment and determination of income after that payment, and reflect the position as understood at the time of writing. Actual interest is computed by the department when your return is processed. Verify current rules or consult a qualified chartered accountant before acting.
